speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to my care. I see you are a newborn; could you tell me if you were born prematurely or if you experienced any complications during delivery?

REQUEST TEST: Full_blood_count, Coagulation_profile
REQUEST TEST: Blood_culture, Urine_culture, Chest_XRay

Please let me know the results of these tests, and describe any specific symptoms your parents have noticed, such as fever, poor feeding, or difficulty breathing.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome. The combination of a continuous heart murmur (likely a PDA), cloudy lenses (cataracts), and non-blanching skin lesions is classic for this triad, which contradicts the previous suggestion of cellulitis. I am confident in this diagnosis based on your description of the physical findings.
